opening: I'm Tyler Jewell, CEO of Akka. In the next few minutes I'll take one AI system from its specification to running it efficiently, on one platform.
slide-four-things: Safe, efficient AI needs four things: factories that build and test it, agents that scale and recover, governance enforced on every interaction, and models matched to every request.
slide-integrate: Today, teams integrate those parts themselves. Orchestration, tracing, evaluations, routing and training are each their own tool, and the gaps between them are where risk and cost hide.
slide-shared: In Akka, those constructs are shared. Agents, controls, evaluations, traces, models and the runtime are one platform, so there is less to build, run and pay for.
slide-spine: It comes as four products: Specify, our AI factories; the Agent SDK; Verify, for governance; and Optimize, for models. Build, run, govern and optimize.
slide-binary: And the whole system compiles into one binary that clusters itself, scales and recovers. Let me show you one system, through all four.
card-build: Build. Akka Specify turns a specification into a service that's built, tested and documented by AI factories.
build-spec: This is a lending system: intake, underwriting, adverse-action notices and contests. It started as a specification, with user stories, requirements and the conditions it has to meet before it ships.
build-docs: Akka's harness agents built, tested and documented this service from that spec. Here is the documentation they generated: how one loan application is underwritten, step by step, across the agents, workflows and entities that do it.
build-components: The components, and how they connect.
build-lifecycle: And every state an application moves through, from intake to decision.
build-oversight: And how a person is brought in: a human event is raised, routed to an officer, and decided within its deadline, or escalated.
build-exit: Every condition the spec sets, like a human decides every adverse action, is checked by a test. I run it, and the condition turns green: specification to proof, before anything is deployed.
card-run: Run. The Agent SDK: agents, orchestration and state, in one runtime that scales and recovers.
run-replay: Here it is running. The underwriting workflow orchestrates identity, credit, affordability and an AI assessor. It pauses durably for a person, retries, and fails over safely, all in one runtime.
run-trace: One request, end to end: the endpoint, the workflow, the agent and its model call, and a guardrail stopping an answer it shouldn't give.
run-agent: An applicant asks for more time. The agent looks up the application, calls a tool, answers, and a judge scores the answer. Because extending a deadline is a lending decision, it goes to a person.
run-components: Under it all is the Akka runtime. This one service is entities, workflows, views, agents and endpoints, compiled into a single binary that clusters, scales and recovers on its own.
run-entity: Every entity is event sourced. Here is one loan application's history, event by event, with its state at each step: held in memory, and durable at the same time.
card-govern: Govern. Akka Verify enforces controls on every AI interaction, and keeps the evidence that they hold.
govern-human: That request is now in front of an officer, with the evidence, the judge's view and a deadline. The decision is recorded against the control that required it.
govern-kinds: Controls come in different kinds. Gates check before an action runs. Sanitizers strip what a model must never see. Guardrails stop an answer before it leaves. Evaluations judge quality. And some decisions go to a person.
govern-sanitizer: Each one leaves a verdict. This sanitizer drops personal information an applicant didn't need to share, before the agent ever takes it in, and its verdicts record that it held.
govern-evals: Evaluations run on live traffic too, scoring every answer the agents give, so quality is measured continuously, not just before release.
govern-officers: And the people are reviewed as well: how long each decision took against its minimum, how often two officers agreed, and where cases were escalated.
govern-halt: If something goes wrong, an officer can halt a scope. Work is referred to people until a second officer agrees to lift it.
govern-controls: Controls come from the regulations that apply, the EU AI Act, fair lending and more, and they're enforced in the running system, not just watched.
govern-evidence: And every verdict, every day, is evidence. Here are a hundred and twenty days of it, with every change of controls marked, ready for an auditor.
card-optimize: Optimize. Every request routed to the right model, for the best price and quality.
optimize-gateway: Every model call goes through one gateway. This is it, live: callers on the left, models on the right. The width of each stream is the tokens flowing, and every exchange is captured.
optimize-costs: So cost is exact: what the AI system cost this week against last, by use case, laid out like a financial statement, with the footnotes an auditor expects.
optimize-price: I can price this week's traffic on a cheaper model, then propose it as a change. Optimize trials it on real traffic and checks quality against the bar before anything rolls out.
optimize-train: You can also train your own small models on your proprietary datasets, on your own GPUs.
optimize-datasets: Training starts with your own data. Datasets are versioned in your own registry, built from your records, so nothing leaves your environment.
optimize-newrun: A run names a base model, a dataset and its settings. Optimize checks the plan and the GPUs it needs before anything starts.
optimize-replay: Here's a training run, replayed: the loss falling step by step as the model learns, until it's ready to evaluate against the model it would replace.
optimize-scores: Every candidate is scored against the model it would replace, on the same evaluation set, before it can serve a single request.
optimize-serve: When a model passes, we serve it on our own inference and send it a canary of one request in ten. Back on the gateway, there it is: the small model taking its share of live traffic.
close: Specified, built, verified and optimized, on one platform. That's Akka. Scale AI, efficiently.
